MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 3, 2011

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission
Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Leckness at 5:02 p.m., on January 3, 2011, at
200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 22, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Ury (arrived at 5:10 p.m.)
  Mayor Leckness

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel—Anticipated Litigation. Potential Litigation
  Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Government Code Section 54956.9. One Case Under

City Council Minutes  1  January 3, 2011
   Consideration.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council did not consider item CS1 as the
circumstances have changed. For item CS2, the City Council agreed, by unanimous vote, to
redraft the City Manager’s contract to clarify the City Manager’s ability to distribute his
compensation. It does not, in any way, increase or change the dollar amount of the contract. The
amended contract will come back to the City Council for formal approval as a Consent Calendar
item.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation to Former Mayor Kelley

  Mayor Leckness presented Council Member Kelley with a gavel plaque for her service as
  Mayor in 2010.

P2.  Opening Remarks from Mayor Leckness

  Mayor Leckness discussed his goals while he serves as Mayor in 2011.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Mauer, M.V.: announced that there are an amazing range of services available at the
Mission Viejo library and he outlined several of the great programs offered.

Dan Avery, M.V.: speaking on behalf of a canine resident named Hunter, he expressed support
for the building of a dog park in Mission Viejo. He further asked Council Member Reardon to
pull the dog park item from the Consent Calendar so two questions can be answered.

Stuart Jasper, M.V.: discussed his appearance before the City Council in December regarding an
appeal and dispute between his two neighbors. He stated that one of the parties presented a false

City Council Minutes  2  January 3, 2011
 document and he wishes to clear his name by notifying the Council that the document was a
forgery and the individual’s words were lies.

Matt Corrigan, M.V.: thanked Mayor Leckness for calling out the importance of maintaining
homeowner values in his opening remarks and stated that he objects to the OCFA’s
recommendation for fire sprinklers in residential dwelling units.

Ron and Donna Langstoffel, M.V.: thanked city staff and the Council Members for supporting
their new Mission Viejo business, Massage Heights.

Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: announced that her son asked to visit the Library several times during
the Christmas break because the programs are very appealing to children.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

16.  Ordinances Adopting the 2010 California Building Code and Fire Code

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report and
  outlined a few minor corrections on pages 2 and 3 of the draft ordinance.

City Council Minutes  4  January 3, 2011
   At the hour of 6:32 p.m., Mayor Leckness opened the public hearing.

  Paula Snyder, OCFA employee, Mission Viejo resident and an HOA Board Member,
  M.V.: discussed the merits of fire sprinklers in homes and urged the Council to vote yes
  on the ordinance.

  John Lusk, M.V.: expressed support for fire sprinklers in new units but stated his
  opposition to requiring fire sprinklers in remodeled units.

  The Council and audience viewed a short video, presented by OCFA, on the benefits of
  residential fire sprinkler systems.

  Assistant Fire Marshall Dennis Grubb, OCFA: discussed the proposed residential fire
  sprinkler requirements and answered questions of the City Council Members.

  Assistant Fire Chief Laura Blaul, OCFA: addressed the Council’s concerns about
  residential fire sprinklers.

  The following expressed their support for the motion as made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury:
  Wendy Bucknum, M.V. and Ramona Acosta, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley to (1) adopt Ordinance 10-XXX, Amending
  Title 8 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code by Adopting by Reference the 2010 Editions
  of the California Building, Plumbing, Electrical and Mechanical Codes, and Related
  Model and Uniform Codes, with Certain Appendices and Amendments Thereto; (2) adopt
  Resolution 11-XX Setting Forth Findings for Required Amendments to the 2010
  California Building Code Relative to Local Climatic, Topographic, and Geologic
  Conditions; (3) adopt Ordinance 10-XXX, Adopting by Reference the 2010 California
  Fire Code, Incorporating the International Fire Code 2009 Edition, with Errata, Including
  Appendices B, BB, and C, and the Referenced Standards, Together with Certain
  Amendments and Deletions; and (4) adopt Resolution 11-XX Setting Forth Findings for
  Required Amendments to the 2010 California Fire Code Relative to Local Climatic,
  Topographic, and Geologic Conditions.

  The motion died for lack of a second.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to (1)
  adopt Ordinance 10-287, Amending Title 8 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code by
  Adopting by Reference the 2010 Editions of the California Building, Plumbing, Electrical
  and Mechanical Codes, and Related Model and Uniform Codes, with Certain Appendices
  and Amendments Thereto; (2) adopt Resolution 11-04 Setting Forth Findings for
  Required Amendments to the 2010 California Building Code Relative to Local Climatic,
  Topographic, and Geologic Conditions; (3) adopted Ordinance 10-288, as amended*,
  Adopting by Reference the 2010 California Fire Code, Incorporating the International

City Council Minutes  5  January 3, 2011
   Fire Code 2009 Edition, with Errata, Including Appendices B, BB, and C, and the
  Referenced Standards, Together with Certain Amendments and Deletions; and (4)
  adopted Resolution 11-05 Setting Forth Findings for Required Amendments to the 2010
  California Fire Code Relative to Local Climatic, Topographic, and Geologic Conditions.

  *Amendment to Ordinance 10-288: remove sections R313.1 and R313.2 which would
  require automatic fire sprinkler systems in new and certain renovated townhouse units
  and in new and some remodeled one-family and two-family dwelling units (pages 21 and
  22 of the agenda report.) Staff was also directed to look at and remove any other
  provisions that would require fire sprinklers in residential units.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness
  ABSENT: None

26.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley commended city staff for the festive holiday decorations. She noted
that the lighting on La Paz Road and at the civic center were beautiful and many residents
contacted her to say how much they appreciated the holiday lights. She also thanked the Mission
Viejo Activities Committee for once again hosting Santa’s Workshop. She was pleased to visit
Santa with her two grandchildren and it was a wonderful effort by the Activities Committee and
another great success. Council Member Kelley reminded residents that the city will host a
Whooping Cough/Pertussis vaccination clinic at the Murray Community Center on January 7,
2011, from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. The clinic is sponsored by the Orange County Health Care
Agency and the vaccines are free. A new law, effective this year, requires all children entering
grades 7 through 12 to submit proof that they have received a Whooping Cough/Pertussis booster
and it is also recommended for adults who have contact with infants under twelve-months of age.
Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of
January is perseverance.

Council Member Reardon

27.  Revision of City Council Meeting Rules of Order and Procedures Permitting
  Members of the Public to Pull Items from the Consent Calendar

  Council Member Reardon presented her report.

  The following spoke in support of the proposal to allow members of the public to pull
  items from the Consent Calendar: Larry Gilbert, M.V.

  The following expressed opposition to the proposal to allow members of the public to
  pull items from the Consent Calendar: Dan Avery, M.V.; Wendy Bucknum, M.V.; and
  Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.

City Council Minutes  12  January 3, 2011
   Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to
  approve the modification of the City Council Meeting Rules of Order and Procedures to
  permit members of the public to remove items from the Consent Calendar for separate
  discussion and vote and to direct the City Clerk to bring back a Resolution, amending
  City Council Meeting Rules of Order and Procedures and Amending the City Council
  Policy Manual.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, Leckness and Ury
  ABSENT: None

Council Member Reardon announced that she spent over two hours on required ethics training
and it really helped her to understand that elected officials are to do above and beyond what is
legal, they are to do what is ethical. She also discussed a conversation she had with City
Attorney Bill Curley regarding her involvement with the YMCA Board of Directors. Mr. Curley
advised her that she must, as a City Council Member, recuse herself from voting on any items
relating to the YMCA and she must also leave the room in order to adhere to the highest ethical
standards. Council Member Reardon asked Council Member Kelley to address some concerns
that she has heard regarding Council Member Kelley’s membership on the OCFA Board of
Directors while she has a son who is employed by the Orange County Fire Authority.

Council Member Kelley stated that this is a non-issue. She is very proud of her firefighter son
who is 32 years-old, married and independent. Her son receives no income from Council
Member Kelley and her voting record on the OCFA Board is public information and transparent.
She announced that she just voted for a 9% pay cut for firefighters and she does not believe there
is an issue, nor do her colleagues on the OCFA Board. Council Member Kelley noted that she
was just recruited by the other Board Members and she was elected as Vice Chair of the OCFA
Board. She encouraged anyone who has questions to contact her and she also asked her City
Council colleagues to let her know if they have a problem with her serving on the OCFA Board.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht stated that she does have a problem with Council Member Kelley
serving on the OCFA Board of Directors with a family member employed by OCFA. Council
Member Schlicht thanked the Orange County Sheriff’s Deputies for responding to her home
when a false alarm sounded over the holidays. She wished everyone a happy New Year and
ended her comments with a quote from Thomas Paine: "When I contemplate the natural dignity
of man; when I feel... for the honor and happiness of its character, I become irritated at the
attempt to govern mankind by force and fraud, as if they were all knaves and fools, and can
scarcely avoid disgust at those who are thus imposed upon."

City Council Minutes  13  January 3, 2011
 Mayor Pro Tem Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Ury announced that he plans to bring an item to the City Council at the next
meeting regarding the targeting of affordable housing units for people who work in Mission
Viejo. He hopes to begin a conversation with his colleagues regarding a potential requirement
that those who provide vital services in Mission Viejo (teachers, paramedics, firefighters, police
officers and nurses) receive priority for the affordable housing units at the two new apartment or
condominium complexes.

Mayor Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness announced that it was nice to see Boy Scout Spencer Bucknum from
Troop 1273 at the meeting this evening. He also reiterated comments about the fantastic holiday
lighting and he noted that he too received many thanks and compliments from residents.

ADJOURNMENT
